headline: Large User Grid Cost Shift Enacted
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, primarily data centers, bear a greater share of their grid infrastructure costs, reducing the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: Virginia Now Makes Data Centers Post $1.5 Million A Megawatt
news_summary: Virginia's utility regulator approved a tariff requiring data centers drawing 25 megawatts or more to sign 14-year contracts, pay for capacity, and post $1.5 million collateral per megawatt. This aims to protect residential ratepayers from costs associated with data center infrastructure and speculative load.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandated
short_summary: This bill requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, increasing transparency regarding their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local communities.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law mandates local water authorities report data center water usage, making the information publicly accessible on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to address concerns about the industry's water consumption and provide transparency.

headline: Local Data Center Siting, Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill empowers localities to require site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including sound profiles and environmental impacts, before approving siting applications.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups.
news_headline: Loudoun Co. Officials Discuss Data Center Noise Mitigation
news_summary: Residents in Loudoun County are experiencing constant noise from data centers, prompting local officials to discuss mitigation efforts and potential changes to noise ordinances. The conflict highlights the growing tension between data center expansion and community quality of life.
